# Dataset documentation

## Source

**Synthetic portfolio, generated by `ml/data/generator.py`** (seeded, fully reproducible).

Why synthetic: no single public dataset has every field in the business brief
(income, debt, savings, expenses, credit score, late payments, existing loans,
home ownership, ...). Common public sets cover only subsets:

| Public dataset | Covers | Missing from brief |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle *Credit Risk Dataset* | age, income, home ownership, employment length, loan amount | credit score, savings, expenses, late-payment counts |
| UCI *German Credit* | savings, employment, credit history, loan amount/duration | income, expenses, credit score; only 1,000 rows |
| *Give Me Some Credit* | utilisation, late payments, debt ratio, income | savings, expenses, loan term |

The generator therefore builds a 10k-customer portfolio with realistic marginal
distributions, correlations (e.g. income vs. credit score, age vs. home
ownership) and injected data-quality problems (missing values, duplicates,
outliers, impossible values, unlabeled rows) so the cleaning pipeline has real
work to do.

> **Limitation:** the default label is drawn from a hand-written logistic risk
> formula. Model metrics on this data demonstrate that the pipeline works; they
> are **not** evidence of performance on real borrowers. Swap in real data
> before drawing business conclusions.

### Using a real dataset

Put a CSV in `data/raw/credit_risk_raw.csv` or call
`load_dataset(path, column_map={"person_age": "age", ...})`. Required columns
are listed in `ml/config.py::REQUIRED_COLUMNS`. Fields a real dataset lacks
must be added or the schema in `ml/config.py` adjusted (features that depend on
them are then skipped or revised).

## Target variable

`default` - `1` = customer defaulted, `0` = repaid. Target-cleaning accepts
`1/0`, `yes/no`, `true/false`, `default/non-default`, `bad/good`; rows with a
missing or unrecognised label are dropped. Default rate is calibrated to about
14% (class imbalance on purpose; balancing is Part 2).

## Data dictionary

| Column | Type | Description | Valid range / levels |
|---|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | str | Unique customer key | `CUST0000001`... |
| `age` | int | Age in years | 18-100 |
| `annual_income` | float | Gross annual income (currency units, USD-like) | > 0 |
| `employment_type` | cat | Employment category | salaried, self_employed, retired, unemployed |
| `employment_years` | float | Tenure in current employment (years) | 0-60 |
| `loan_amount` | float | Requested loan principal | > 0 |
| `loan_term_months` | int | Requested loan duration | 1-480 |
| `credit_score` | int | Bureau-style score | 300-850 |
| `monthly_debt_payment` | float | Monthly payments on existing debt incl. mortgage, excl. rent | >= 0 |
| `credit_limit` | float | Total revolving credit limit | >= 0 |
| `revolving_balance` | float | Current revolving balance | >= 0 |
| `savings_balance` | float | Liquid savings | >= 0 |
| `monthly_expenses` | float | Living expenses per month, excl. debt payments | >= 0 |
| `num_existing_loans` | int | Count of open loans | 0-50 |
| `num_late_payments` | int | Late payments in the observation window | 0-100 |
| `repayment_history` | cat | Qualitative repayment record | excellent, good, fair, poor |
| `home_ownership` | cat | Housing status | rent, mortgage, own, other |
| `default` | int | **Target** | 0 / 1 |

## Assumptions

1. Monetary values share one currency and are comparable across customers.
2. `monthly_debt_payment` covers existing obligations only; the *requested* loan is handled separately via `loan_payment_to_income`.
3. `num_late_payments` and `repayment_history` describe the same observation window, before the loan decision (no leakage from the outcome).
4. Out-of-range values (e.g. age 150) are entry errors and become missing, not clipped.
5. Missingness is treated as potentially informative, so the preprocessing pipeline adds missing-value indicators.
